item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

Alright, so this skip mentions that whatever is in the box is close to escape in the recovered document. Game Day Phase 1 features said escape, or at least a version of it, without going into real detail as to what is inside. Additionally, SCP-052 features an individual who claims to know what is in SCP-699, so an inline link between the two is not so out of line. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

2/7/2466 Escape imminent. Experimental Containment Procedure “T” to be implemented immediately. We believe the inhabitants of the receiving timeline lack the [report damaged] and will for many years.

To this:

2/7/2466 Escape imminent. Experimental Containment Procedure “T” to be implemented immediately. We believe the inhabitants of the receiving timeline lack the [report damaged] and will for many years.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
That is what you're supposed to think.

However, if you read Game Day, you'll see there is an alternative possibility:

699 is an infiltrator, and the report sent with it is a cover story, to induce the Foundation to keep it. It's not contained at all, and whatever is in the box can let itself out whenever it wants. It's waiting for something that hasn't happened yet, so is content to stay put in the box. The "impossible to open" part is not designed as containment, but to keep the Foundation from messing around with it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Yes…eek! A Thing From The Future (or someone's future, at least). I thought it had a good enough hook to write it up, even though I know "stuff from the future" is pretty much a discredited trope around here. Enough people said they liked the concept in the chat/forum for me to go with it…totally expected a few down votes, since I know some folks here believe we have enough stuff from the future, especially from new writers.

Good point, thunderbird…I am going to add something to the partial report that came with the object to imply that it was more powerful wherever it was sent from than it appears to be here. Trying to balance the too explicit vs. too vague aspect has been difficult, since both lead to "not creepy enough". It's definitely not Keter here (and is only Euclid because no one is quite sure of the extent of its powers).
